description: Rise, set, transit and twilight times for 5 sites x 6 dates x 6 objects.
notes: Time: every instant is its calendar value read as UT1 (DUT1 = 0, the same assumption as LodestarKit's JulianDate(date:)); TT = UT1 + DeltaT with DeltaT from Skyfield's builtin tables (IERS daily values 1973-01-02..2027-01-23, Stephenson/Morrison/Hohenkerk splines and parabola elsewhere). No IERS download, no polar motion.
Window: local noon of 'date' to the next local noon, where local noon is 12:00:00 UT minus longitude/15 hours (rounded to whole seconds). Events are searched strictly inside the window.

Altitude: topocentric, geometric (no refraction) altitude of the body's centre (Skyfield apparent place, WGS84 vertical). A crossing is an instant where altitude - h0 changes sign: kind 'rise' = upward, 'set' = downward; the same kinds are used for dawn (rise) and dusk (set) at the twilight thresholds.
h0 (degrees): stars and planets -0.5667; Sun -0.8333; Sun twilights -6 (civil), -12 (nautical), -18 (astronomical). Crossings are resolved to 1 ms.

WARNING (Moon): DESIGN.md section 4.1 prescribes h0 = 0.7275*pi - 0.5667 deg for the Moon. That is Meeus' threshold for the GEOCENTRIC altitude of the Moon's centre; applied to the topocentric altitude, as for every other body here, it puts rise and set about pi (~0.95 deg) too high: about 4 minutes off at the equator, 5-10 minutes at 34-52 degrees latitude, up to 16 minutes at 70 degrees, as JPL Horizons and the US Naval Observatory confirm (see README.md).

moon.horizon implements the DESIGN.md text literally: topocentric centre altitude vs h0 = 0.7275*pi - 0.5667 deg, pi = asin(6378.14 km / geocentric distance) at the crossing instant (h0 is recorded per crossing).

moon.horizon_upper_limb is the real event: topocentric centre altitude vs h0 = -0.5667 deg - asin(1737.4 km / topocentric distance), i.e. the upper limb on the horizon after 34 arcminutes of refraction (USNO and JPL Horizons definition). Meeus' geocentric formulation (geocentric altitude vs 0.7275*pi - 0.5667 deg) gives the same instants to within 3 seconds.
A list with no crossings carries always_up or always_down (the altitude stays at least 0.05 deg from h0 for the whole window).

transits: upper culminations, i.e. local maxima of the topocentric geometric altitude, with that altitude in degrees; culminations below the horizon are listed too. For the Sun, Moon and planets the time can differ from the meridian passage by seconds (Sun, planets) to many minutes (Moon at high latitude). A window can hold zero (Moon) or, rarely, two transits.
